title: Rollouts: persist published changelog reference on version changes
author: Chloe Martin
body:
Context: With the model changelog generator landing, we want Rollouts to be able to show customers exactly which published changelog entry corresponded to a rollout decision at the time it happened. Today Rollouts only store model_id/version_id and the UI tries to link to “latest” release note content, which is incorrect for (a) corrections/supersedes, (b) backfilled notes, and (c) cases where a version is republished with a clarified summary.

What this PR does: Adds integration hooks so that whenever a rollout transitions traffic to a specific model version, we resolve the currently published changelog entry for that model_id+version_id and persist an immutable reference on the rollout event record. The Rollouts UI (and export) can then link to the exact entry that was published at the time of change.

High-level changes: (1) New optional fields on rollout_event: changelog_entry_id, changelog_url_snapshot, changelog_published_at_snapshot. (2) Control plane resolver call on rollout event creation: GET /v1/changelog/entries:resolve?model_id=...&version_id=... (returns the published entry id/url if one exists). (3) Rollouts read path now returns these fields; UI can prefer snapshot link over recomputing “current” link. (4) Feature flag: console.rollouts_changelog_snapshot (default off). When off, no resolver call is made and fields remain null.

Behavior notes: If there is no published changelog entry at rollout time, we persist nulls and the UI shows “Release notes not yet published” (same as current). If an entry is later superseded/corrected, the rollout continues to link to the original entry (auditability), and the entry page itself shows its superseded status.

Why snapshot the URL: console/docs can change routing; we store both entry_id (canonical) and url snapshot (best-effort convenience). The UI uses entry_id to reconstruct a current URL if the snapshot is missing.

Testing: Added unit tests for resolver call + persistence, plus an integration-ish test using fixtures to simulate (a) no entry, (b) published entry, (c) superseded entry after the fact. Also verified in staging with the generator feed from PR #18805.

Follow-ups: Backfill for historical rollout events is intentionally out of scope (we don’t have reliable publish-time mapping pre-migration). If needed, we can add an admin backfill later that only fills changelog_entry_id where an exact match can be proven.

Refs: ENG-4927 (Console rollouts changelog tab integration) + ENG-4926 (generator publish targets). Supports enterprise change-management requests asking for immutable links (SUP-18421).
commits: control-plane/rollouts: add changelog snapshot fields to RolloutEvent schema
rollouts-service: resolve published changelog entry at event creation (flagged)
rollouts read APIs: expose changelog_entry_id + url snapshot
tests: add fixtures for resolve endpoint + supersede behavior
docs/dev: update rollout event contract notes for console consumers
ci_summary: Checks: build-and-unit (pass), api-contract (pass), lint (pass), integration-staging-fixtures (pass). Note: first run failed on api-contract due to missing OpenAPI example for new fields; fixed in 9b2a3d1 and re-run passed.
conversation:
Paula Mendes: Can we confirm the UX expectation here? For enterprise audits we need the link to be stable even if we publish a corrected note later. Also please make sure the UI copy doesn’t imply the version changed again when the note is superseded.

Chloe Martin (author): Yep—this stores the entry_id at the time of the rollout event. If later superseded, the entry page will show “Superseded by …” but the rollout still points at the original. UI can render a small badge if the entry itself is superseded (separate PR on the frontend).

Jada Williams: Re: workflow states—what if the entry is in_review but not published at the exact moment the rollout happens? We should not leak drafts.

Chloe Martin: Resolver endpoint only returns entries with status=published. Draft/in_review return 404-like “no published entry”. We store nulls and the UI shows “not yet published”.

Ethan Park: Concern about adding a synchronous dependency on changelog service during rollout writes. Any timeouts/retries? We should avoid blocking the rollout decision path.

Chloe Martin: Good call. Implementation is best-effort with a 150ms timeout; failure is swallowed and we proceed with nulls. Added a metric rollouts_changelog_resolve_errors_total and a histogram for latency. Also gated behind feature flag for staged rollout.

Quentin Harris: For the url snapshot, are we storing a docs URL or a control plane URL? Docs URLs can change.

Chloe Martin: We store the canonical control plane public URL (api.redwoodinference.com/changelog/entries/{id}) and let console redirect or render. Snapshot remains best-effort; entry_id is the canonical piece.

Dylan Brooks: Please ensure migration is backwards compatible and doesn’t lock rollouts table too long.

Chloe Martin: Migration adds nullable columns with no defaults; tested on staging with ~12M events, completes in <2s. No backfill. Included in migration notes.

Paula Mendes: Approved assuming the UI copy change lands soon.

Jada Williams: Approved.

Ethan Park: Approved after the timeout/metrics changes.

Quentin Harris: Approved.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Chloe Martin. Squash commit: 4f8c2e91b3 ("Rollouts: persist published changelog reference on version changes").
